## Call chains reaching `i915_pm_suspend`

There are two PM-table entries that point directly to `i915_pm_suspend`.

### System suspend

```text
PCI PM core
  -> i915_pm_ops.suspend
  -> i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)
  -> kdev_to_i915(kdev)
       -> dev_get_drvdata(kdev)
       -> to_i915(drm)
       -> struct drm_i915_private *i915
  -> i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
  -> to_i915(dev)
       -> struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv
  -> display = dev_priv->display
  -> intel_display_driver_suspend(display)
```

Relevant locations:

- `i915_driver.c:1392-1404` — `i915_pm_suspend`
- `i915_driver.c:1103-1147` — `i915_drm_suspend`
- `i915_display_driver.c:684-706` — `intel_display_driver_suspend`

Within `i915_drm_suspend`, the display suspend call is:


at `i915_driver.c:1120`.

```text
PCI PM core

  -> i915_pm_suspend(kdev)
  -> i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
  -> intel_display_driver_suspend(dev_priv->display)
```

The relevant assignment is:

```c

```

at `i915_driver.c:1745`.

Thus, the distinct PCI PM callback entries that reach `i915_pm_suspend` are:

| PM callback | Assigned function | Chain continues to |
|---|---|---|
| `.suspend` | `i915_pm_suspend` | `i915_drm_suspend` → `intel_display_driver_suspend` |

There is no `i915_pm_runtime_suspend` symbol in this source tree. The runtime callback is:

## `dev_priv` data flow to display suspend

The exact data flow is:

```text
struct device *kdev
  |
  | kdev_to_i915(kdev)
  |   drm = dev_get_drvdata(kdev)
  |   return to_i915(drm)
  v
struct drm_i915_private *i915
  |
  | i915->drm
  v
i915_drm_suspend(struct drm_device *dev)
  |
  | dev_priv = to_i915(dev)
  |   container_of(dev, struct drm_i915_private, drm)
  v
struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv
  |
  | display = dev_priv->display
  v
struct intel_display *display
  |
  | intel_display_driver_suspend(display)
  v
display->drm
  |
  | drm_atomic_helper_suspend(display->drm)
```

The important point is that `dev_priv` is not passed directly into the display routine. It is used to obtain `dev_priv->display`; the called function receives only the `struct intel_display *display` pointer.
